doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

title: Wilbur Campbell's Ike Day story and Ike's generosity and strip-joint shows
summary: Ike humbles Wilbur Campbell at the Ritz, teaches Ware how to play shows, and works the Calumet City strip clubs.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: But even then, some people seemed to have had more than others. Like Wilbur Campbell likes to tell the story about Ike Day.
Oh yes. Wilbur said he went in and sat in and he'd been practicing; he just knew he was ready to play with the group. And he said he went down to this place called

The Ritz, and there was a tenor player around called that Dave Young had -- I think he had a sextet then -- a popular place -- and Wilbur said he'd sit in, and Dave turned around and said, and screamed, he said, "Ike, come up here and play some time." And Wilbur said he was so mad he'd get up off the drums and go home and practiced.

Well, Ike was like that -- he'd show you anything. He showed me a whole lot of things. He showed me how to play shows. Ike -- I think he lived out in Harvey, so that was close to Calumet City where they had all these strip joints, you know, like in Vegas -- and these dancers and what not would strip. Strip had come in with big band arrangements. They might have 4 pieces out there, or they might have 5, some only 3, but they got 16 pieces arrangements, and they let you play. Ike was in demand out there like mad.
He was playing all those kinds of music?

He'd play everything. The man was a genius. There's no drummer, I think, in the country that came to Chicago and never met Ike or heard of him. I'll tell you, I mean, all of them -- Klook, old man Max, Joe Jones ...
So in addition to being -- to keeping time, as you would say, he was ...
He was all over. The man was phenomenal. He was something.
